title: Legal Gateways and Data Protection
summary: The legal bases that permit sharing between authorities and firms and between firms, and how to embed data protection, confidentiality and tipping-off safeguards from the outset.
contentGaps: Written as part of a programme: Aim and Purpose is the module's one-line description; audience, prior knowledge and core reading come from the programme

sections.Aim and Purpose: The legal bases that permit sharing between authorities and firms and between firms, and how to embed data protection, confidentiality and tipping-off safeguards from the outset.
Learning Objectives: Identify the legal gateways for public-to-private and private-to-private sharing
Apply data protection principles, including necessity and proportionality
Manage confidentiality, tipping-off and liability risks
Syllabus: Statutory gateways, safe harbours and information-sharing provisions
Data protection principles and impact assessments
Confidentiality, tipping-off and protection from liability
Intended Audience: FIU heads, partnership managers and senior analysts
Law-enforcement leads for economic crime, fraud and terrorist financing
Policy, legal and data protection officers advising on information-sharing arrangements
sections.Useful Prior Knowledge and Experience: Some experience of financial intelligence, investigation or AML/CFT policy is helpful. No legal or data protection expertise is required.
Core Reading: FATF (2017), Guidance on Private Sector Information Sharing
FATF (2021), Stocktake on Data Pooling, Collaborative Analytics and Data Protection
FATF (2022), Partnering in the Fight Against Financial Crime: Data Protection, Technology and Private Sector Information Sharing
Egmont Group (2013), Principles for Information Exchange Between Financial Intelligence Units
